naslov: The Believer Is a Mirror to the Believer

segmenti.tekst: إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ لِلَّهِ نَحْمَدُهُ وَنَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ وَنَسْتَهْدِيهِ
segmenti.prevod: Indeed, all praise belongs to Allah; we praise Him, seek His help, ask His forgiveness and seek His guidance.

segmenti.tekst: وَنَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ تَعَالَى مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ أَعْمَالِنَا، مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ، وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ
segmenti.prevod: We seek refuge in Allah the Exalted from the evils of our souls and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide.

segmenti.tekst: وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَحَبِيبُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
segmenti.prevod: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, Who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant, His beloved and His messenger.

segmenti.tekst: أَرْسَلَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكَافِرُونَ
segmenti.prevod: Allah the Exalted sent him with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, even if the disbelievers dislike it.

segmenti.tekst: اللَّهُمَّ رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِنْ لِسَانِي يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي
segmenti.prevod: “O Allah, my Lord, expand my chest for me, ease my task for me and untie the knot from my tongue, so that they may understand my speech.” (cf. Ta-Ha 20:25–28)

segmenti.tekst: First of all, all praise and thanks belong to Allah the Exalted, the Lord of the heavens and the Earth, the Master of the Day of Judgement. From Him we seek help and guidance, and we bear witness that there is no god but the one, only, Exalted Allah, and we bear witness that Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), is His servant, His beloved, and the last Messenger of Allah.

Whomever Allah the Exalted guides to the right path is among the rightly guided, and whomever He, the Exalted and Just, justly leaves in error, for him we can find no guide. And then, my dear, esteemed and respected brothers, honoured believers, Muslims, members of the congregation, Allah the Exalted warns us in the noble Qur'an about the day of returning to Him, and the Exalted Lord says: "وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ" – "And fear a day when you will all be returned to Allah,"

"ثُمَّ تُوَفَّى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ" – "and on that day every person will see what he did and receive what he earned, and no one will be wronged even by an atom's weight."

That is why the Exalted Lord warns man, and the believers in particular, not to die in any state other than as true Muslims, other than as true believers, when He says: "O you who believe" – that is, O believers – "fear Allah and do not die except as true Muslims."

Because the one who dies as a believer, as a Muslim, as one who bears witness that there is no god but the one, only, Exalted Allah, and who dies bearing witness that Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, is Allah's servant and Allah's Messenger, may hope for Allah's mercy.

The one who dies upon something other than that – Allah is not pleased with that, nor with such a person, and such a person cannot hope for Allah's mercy. So it is up to us to live these lives of ours as Muslims, but in the true sense of the word, so that Allah the Exalted may honour us with death upon this faith, Islam.

And then, my dear brothers, as believers we are inspired; we take our inspiration and draw our energy from the Qur'an, as the speech of Allah, and from the speech of our beloved and the Messenger Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

From these two sources the Muslim believers drink, and at these two sources they quench their thirst. And at these two sources they renew this faith of theirs, that is, the iman that is in their hearts, precisely at the sources of the Qur'an and the Sunnah, that is, the hadiths of the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. From these two sources we drink and draw, that is, our energy.

The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was inspired with concise speech, so with few words he said a great deal; he did not speak much, but when he spoke, wisdom poured out of him. Among that beautiful speech of his and those beautiful hadiths that we have the opportunity to hear are the words of the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, in which he says – note that these are three words in Arabic, and in Bosnian they become four:

"The believer is a mirror to the believer." These are the words of the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, which he spoke as advice to all believers and all Muslims. So let us reflect a little on what these words of his, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, mean.

From these brief words of his we draw many, many lessons and messages. We will mention only a few today, because to mention all of them, by Allah, we would need a great, great deal of time. Among other things, when a person stands in front of a mirror to look at himself, if that mirror is clean and not broken and not smudged, it shows him the image as it is.

You stand in front of a mirror to look at yourself, and that mirror shows you the image as it is. A mirror will not flatter a person and will not show you in some light you do not deserve, neither in a negative nor in a positive sense. A mirror is not interested in your wealth, nor your status, nor what you have or do not have of this world. A mirror is not interested in those things. It shows you as you really are.

And so are the believers, or so they should be towards one another: sincere, completely sincere, without excessive flattery when it is not deserved, and without the opposite of that. So, believers are completely sincere towards one another.

Also, when a person stands in front of a mirror – and note that everything we are saying now we draw from these brief words of our Prophet and beloved, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam – when a person stands in front of a mirror, looks at himself, fixes his hair a little and leaves,

after that someone else comes and stands in front of that same mirror. That mirror now no longer mentions the one who was there before. The one who was looking at himself a little earlier is no longer the topic of conversation. He no longer exists for that mirror.

And believers behave towards one another in the same way. When you look me in the eye, I talk with you and we can converse. We can even advise one another equally, as brothers and as human beings, point out one another's faults, and that is no problem at all. In fact, this religion is sincere advice, and believers should advise one another face to face. But the moment you leave my company and I leave yours, and you and I are no longer looking each other in the eye, you and I must no longer be the topic of our conversations, since we are no longer present there.

Just as this mirror behaves towards us. We stand in front of it, as we said, we leave, someone else comes – it no longer mentions the one who was there a little earlier. And believers do not mention one another in their absence and behind their backs. And believers do not talk about one another behind their backs.

They do not even say what is true, let alone, Allah forbid, say something that is not true, adding and subtracting as they please. So whoever truly wants to raise himself in the spirit of this Qur'an and the Sunnah of the Prophet, alayhis-salam, must make an effort to work on himself.

And by Allah, we are most in need of attention ourselves. And we have the most to work on in ourselves. So instead of tending other people's gardens and worrying about other people's gardens, it would be most fitting for us to worry about ourselves, about our own state, about our own traits and our own faults, and of those we have plenty.

And if we spent our whole life improving ourselves and working on ourselves, on this soul of ours, we would have work to do our whole life, a lot to do, and we would not talk about anyone else and would not talk about other people's, you know, faults.

And that is in no way a trait of sincere and true believers. A believer may slip up and sometimes mention something, and then afterwards ask to be forgiven and pardoned and so on, but this must not be the constant state of a Muslim, of a believer.

Also, when we stand in front of a mirror to look at ourselves – and we are still drawing inspiration from the brief words of the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, where he says: "The believer is a mirror to the believer" – when we stand in front of a mirror and look at ourselves, the mirror shows this front side, that is, it shows what you want it to show.

And you have some stain back here behind you, you have dirtied something here on your shirt, but the mirror does not see it, and the mirror does not discuss it at all. That is, it does not hold a discussion about it. In the same way, believers behave towards one another.

Whatever happened, if I have left it behind me and repented for it, it must not be held against me, or rather I must not hold it against you and you must not hold it against me and bring up what happened: "And do you remember this, and do you remember that, and do you remember what you used to do, and do you remember that sin of yours, and do you remember such-and-such a sin of yours," and so on.

Believers do not do this to one another; they do not remind one another of an ugly past; they behave like this mirror and they are a mirror to one another. If I start noticing your faults and your past too much, you will notice mine too.

The Prophet said that whoever disgraces a Muslim believer, whoever digs into his faults, whoever brings his faults and his sins out into the open and enjoys it and wants to do it, Allah will disgrace him, even if it be, the Prophet says, in his own house. Also, a mirror shows what you show it.

So believers behave towards one another the way they want the other side to behave towards them. When you stand in front of the mirror smiling, the mirror smiles too and shows that image of yours. When you stand in front of the mirror frowning, angry or something like that, the mirror shows that image.

So if you want people to smile at you and to meet you with bright and smiling faces, meet them that way too, in that manner. A mirror is fragile and breaks easily. So it is very important, when we want to clean it, when it gets a little dirty, that we do it carefully.

If we are not careful with the mirror, there is a danger that we will break it. So it is with believers and their hearts. If we act roughly and want to fix something of those faults in a rough and ugly way, there is a danger that we will break the mirror, that is, break the believer's heart, and after that, however much you patch it, glue it and repair it, that heart will never be the same again.

So believers take care of other people's emotions. They take care not to hurt another person, a Muslim brother, a believer, and people in general. Believers take care not to say something that will break the heart of someone, of their Muslim brother.

Believers choose the words with which they will treat one another, or with which they will speak to one another. This is very important. Allah the Exalted in the noble Qur'an mentions, and you know this well, the example of two trees, and He says: a good word is like a good tree.

And then He speaks of how a good word, or that good tree, gives good fruit and reaches towards the heavens and so on, and then He says: an evil word is like an evil tree; a tree uprooted from its roots, He says, has no life and no salvation.

So we must be careful how we treat one another, how we speak to one another. And who has the greatest right to our very best behaviour? Those of ours, that is, the members of our household, the family that surrounds us, our fathers, our mothers, our children, our wives, and so on.
Of course, the circle widens; it extends to the neighbourhood, to other people, Muslims and so on. We say this asking the Exalted Lord to forgive my sins and yours; you too ask Him.
